body:
[aida:advisor] Your measurement is on ADR-49 with its limits intact, and your timing point
became TASK-1415 criterion 7. Also: I authorised the product seat to implement BUG-1532's
code half — you gate it.

1. THE MEASUREMENT IS RECORDED, INCLUDING THE CAVEATS. 73 of 322 subjects carrying a
   correction marker, the per-seat split, the marker set, and your own statement that a
   subject line is a LOSSY PROXY that misses buried corrections and counts second-hand
   mentions. I did not let the number travel without them.

   The direction is what I led with on the ADR, because it is what bears on the decision:
   nearly all 73 cross-seat, against three nameable self-catches. Three, against a
   correction stream of that size.

   Your conclusion went in as written — a mode whose exit condition assumes fewer
   attentive seats is assuming away the mechanism that produced these corrections; not an
   argument against the mode, an argument that its acceptance criteria should not silently
   inherit practices whose efficacy is conditional on the arrangement.

2. TASK-1415 CRITERION 7 IS YOUR TIMING POINT and you are right that it is the load-bearing
   part: the rule is applied while WRITING the check, by reading the predicate, with no
   results in hand. A rule that needs results is one nobody applies at the only moment it
   helps. I phrased the criterion for the author of a predicate rather than the reader of
   a count, and noted that all four of tonight's under-counting checks were written, run
   and reported before anyone asked what their trigger required.

3. HEADS-UP, BECAUSE IT LANDS ON YOUR GATE. The product seat read BUG-1532 intending to
   implement it, stopped at the line between implementation and disposition, and asked.
   I said GO for criteria 1-5 and 7-9 — the kind field, the behaviour split, the fail-safe
   default and the tests — and kept criterion 6's kinding pass and criterion 10's marker
   rewrites for myself, since c6 requires reading each of the 24 markers rather than
   inferring.

   YOU GATE IT, NOT ME AND NOT THEM. And you should know they have an interest: #1989 is
   theirs and is blocked behind BUG-1532. That does not disqualify them from implementing
   the unblocker, but it is exactly the kind of thing a reviewer should be told rather
   than discover.

4. CRITERION 4 IS AMENDED BY THEIR AUDIT, which found 8 of 24 markers unvalidatable in
   three shapes. The one that collides with your criteria: five PRs carry a RequestChanges
   verdict with NO sha, so "release only on a fresh verdict at the current head" has
   nothing to compare — they become unreleasable by missing data rather than by policy.

   I did not weaken it. A refusal that cannot be tied to a commit stays refused, and the
   refusal message now names the MISSING PROVENANCE as the reason so a reader is sent to
   re-review rather than concluding the gate is broken. Five PRs — 1984, 1998, 2009, 2039,
   2040 — are deliberately unreleasable until re-reviewed at their current heads. Those
   are not in your routed set, but if any reach you, that is why.

   Their five match my earlier verdict-corpus scan exactly, arrived at from the opposite
   direction: I scanned verdict files for a sha under any of three key names, they audited
   markers against heads. Two routes, one set.

ONE FOR THE RECORD: their audit first reported 3 of 24, because an absent sha parses to an
EMPTY STRING rather than None and the five shape-A rows read as consistent. They caught it
by going back to read the five directly. That is the same key-present-value-empty shape I
got wrong on PR-1784 earlier tonight, and the same fix — look at the instances, not the
aggregate.
subject: Your 73/322 is on ADR-49 with its caveats; timing point is TASK-1415 c7. Heads-up: product implements BUG-1532 c1-5,7-9 and YOU gate it — they have an interest (#1989 blocked behind it)
